test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 24 Dec, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following statements about the principal focus of a spherical mirror is/are correct?

(a) It always lies midway between the pole and the centre of curvature.

(b) Its position depends on the size of the mirror.

(c) It always lies at the centre of curvature.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only (a)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **principal focus** of a **spherical mirror** is the point where rays of light parallel to the principal axis converge (in a concave mirror) or appear to diverge from (in a convex mirror) after reflection.
 
• For a **concave mirror**, the principal focus lies midway between the **pole** (the center of the mirror's surface) and the **center of curvature** (the center of the sphere of which the mirror is a part).
 
• The **position of the principal focus** does not depend on the size of the mirror. It is always at a fixed distance, which is half the radius of curvature (i.e., focal length = radius of curvature / 2).
 
• For a **convex mirror**, the principal focus is also located midway between the pole and the center of curvature but appears to be behind the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Its position depends on the size of the mirror**__

 __
 
• This statement is incorrect because the position of the principal focus is determined by the radius of curvature and not by the size of the mirror.
 
• The focal length remains constant for a given mirror regardless of its size.
 
 
 
• **It always lies at the centre of curvature**__
 
 
• This statement is incorrect because the principal focus is distinct from the center of curvature. The center of curvature is twice the distance from the mirror compared to the principal focus.
